hints: Focus on finding a chiral centre, a carbon atom bonded to four completely different atoms or groups.
Look closely at the carbon carrying the chlorine atom in each molecule and list its four groups.
Check which chlorine-bearing carbon has no repeated groups, with a methyl on one side and a branched group on the other.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes a molecule chiral**

A molecule is chiral if it has at least one chiral centre. That is a carbon with four different groups attached, so it has no plane of symmetry and is non-superimposable on its mirror image.

**Examine the carbon with chlorine in each compound**

Write them out quickly:
$$\text{A: ClCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)}_2$$
$$\text{B: CH}_3\text{C(Cl)(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
$$\text{C: CH}_3\text{CH(Cl)CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$$
$$\text{D: CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(Cl)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
Now ask for each C-Cl carbon: are all four groups different?

**Spot the only carbon with four different groups**

In C, carbon-2 is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{Cl}$, $\text{CH}_3$, and $\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$. All four are different, so this carbon is chiral and the whole molecule is chiral.

options.A: Incorrect. 1-chloro-3-methylbutane is $\text{ClCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$. C-1 has two H atoms, and C-3 has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so no carbon has four different groups.
options.B: Incorrect. 2-chloro-2-methylbutane is $\text{CH}_3\text{C(Cl)(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. C-2 has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups plus Cl and ethyl, so it is not a chiral centre.
options.C: Correct. 2-chloro-3-methylbutane is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(Cl)CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$. C-2 is attached to H, Cl, $\text{CH}_3$, and $\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$, four different groups, so it is a chiral centre and the molecule is chiral.
options.D: Incorrect. 3-chloropentane is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(Cl)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. C-3 has H, Cl, and two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ ethyl groups, so it is symmetrical and achiral. This is a common trap when students see a central Cl and assume chirality.
